data.body:
Independent AC verification against merged `0033662b5534` ("Assert every EBS mount actually took"),
in a fresh worktree off `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 0033662b5534 HEAD` OK,
`rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev 0033662b5534` resolves this ticket). All four boxes ticked on
evidence; nothing was weakened to make a box tickable.

- **AC1 — HOLDS.** `require_mounted` (`infra/terraform/user_data.sh`) runs `mountpoint -q "$1"`
  and returns non-zero with a stderr message on failure. It is called from inside
  `mount_ebs_volume` after `mount -a` (`# ASSERT-MOUNT-TOOK`, `return 4`), so BOTH call sites get
  it — `/var/gerrit` and gate scratch — and the `/var/gerrit` branch now FATALs with "volume … is
  not in service at /var/gerrit -- refusing to run Gerrit on the ROOT filesystem". The asymmetry
  the ticket reported is closed by construction rather than by copying the guard.
- **AC2 — HOLDS, and the seed is genuine.**
  `test_a_silently_skipped_nofail_mount_is_refused` runs the shipped shell with `mount` stubbed to
  exit 0 without mounting (`mount_mode="skips"`) and asserts non-zero.
  `test_removing_the_mount_assertion_restores_the_silent_success` drops the `ASSERT-MOUNT-TOOK`
  line and asserts the SAME scenario returns 0 — so the guard is provably load-bearing, not
  incidental. `test_the_gerrit_data_volume_gets_the_same_assertion_as_gate_scratch` runs the skip
  scenario for both mount points.
- **AC3 — HOLDS.** `test_a_genuine_mount_error_is_distinguishable_from_a_silent_skip` asserts the
  two failures differ in BOTH exit code (3 vs 4) and stderr text ("mount -a reported an ERROR
  while mounting …" vs "… is NOT a mount point after a CLEAN mount -a -- its nofail fstab entry
  was skipped silently"), and that the skip wording does not leak into the error case.
- **AC4 — HOLDS.** `infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh` exists, mode 755, defaults to
  `/var/gerrit /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. Portable by inspection: plain shell + util-linux with
  a `/proc/mounts` fallback, no AWS API call, no CI-provider trigger — the only occurrence of
  "IMDS"/"CI" in the file is the comment explaining that it depends on neither. It reports three
  states (mounted / not mounted / cannot determine) and distinguishes an absent directory from the
  dangerous present-directory-on-root case. Covered by
  `test_the_running_host_check_{exists_and_is_executable,names_both_volumes_by_default,fails_on_a_plain_directory,passes_when_the_volume_is_mounted}`
  plus the fallback tests. `infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md` step 4b now points at it, covers
  both volumes, and says plainly not to treat "Gerrit responds" as evidence.

Verification run in this worktree: `pytest tests/unit/test_user_data_device_resolution_d614.py
tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` → **49 passed**. Shell gates clean:
`scripts/check_shellcheck.py` rc=0, `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py` rc=0. No production
host was touched and no terraform was applied.
